claim.pdf_says: MERGE general format (14.9.24.2), COLLATING SEQUENCE alternative 2 is a brace carrying CHOICE INDICATOR bars just inside it: '{ | FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 | }' over '{ | FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2 | }' -- i.e. a tall '{' followed by a tall vertical bar on the left, and a tall vertical bar followed by the closing '}' on the right, enclosing the two FOR lines.
claim.why_it_matters: The vertical bars are the 5.2.6.4 choice indicator: with them, BOTH 'FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1' and 'FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2' may be specified, each at most once, in any order. Without them a brace around stacked alternatives means EXACTLY ONE. The transcription therefore makes 'COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alpha-1 FOR NATIONAL IS alpha-2' -- the normal case for a MERGE keyed on both alphanumeric and national items, and the case General rule 5a on page 660 explicitly describes -- look illegal, and would drive a compiler to reject legal source.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by direct inspection of the rendered page at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v687/spec_p687.png, printed page 657 = PDF page 687), zoomed 5x on both inner delimiter columns.

WHAT THE PRINTED GLYPHS ARE. Left column of the COLLATING SEQUENCE group, reading left to right: the tall outer '[' bracket (straight stroke with a horizontal foot), then 'COLLATING SEQUENCE', then a tall CURLY '{' (the two-alternative selector), then -- one line lower, spanning only the two FOR lines -- a second, SHORTER CURLY '{' immediately followed by a perfectly STRAIGHT vertical stroke with no serif, no foot, and no curl at either end. Right column, reading left to right after 'alphabet-name-1': a matching perfectly STRAIGHT vertical stroke, then a CURLY '}' closing the inner group, then the taller CURLY '}' closing the two-alternative selector, then the straight stroke with a horizontal foot that closes the outer ']' bracket. The two straight strokes are unmistakably distinct in shape from every brace on the page (which are drawn with the font's curled brace glyph) and from the bracket (which has feet). They are 5.2.6.4 choice-indicator bars, positioned just INSIDE the inner brace pair: '{ | ... | }'. The claim's description of the printed figure is exact.

WHAT THE MARKDOWN IS. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 28272-28276 (workunit page-687.md lines 21-23) reproduce the group as an ASCII-art stack with inner braces on each FOR line and NO bar characters anywhere. The claim quotes those three lines verbatim, including trailing spacing. Neither bar is present on an adjacent line, in a figure note, or anywhere else in the 14.9.24 section -- I checked the whole MERGE block (lines 28255-28300) and grepped the file for '5.2.6.4' / 'choice indicator' figure notes; page 687 has none.

WHY IT IS NORMATIVE, NOT FORMATTING. 5.2.6.4 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 2703) states: 'Choice indicators are a pair of bars, |, that enclose a portion of a general format. When enclosed by braces, one or more of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative shall be specified only once. ... The alternatives may be specified in any order.' Dropping the bars converts a one-or-more-in-any-order group into a plain brace, which per 5.2.6.1/5.2.6.3 selects EXACTLY ONE. So the transcription forbids 'COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS a-1 FOR NATIONAL IS a-2'. That combination is not hypothetical: 14.9.24.4 general rule 5a (PDF page 690 = printed page 660) reads 'The collating sequence associated with alphabet-name-1 applies to key data items of class alphabetic and alphanumeric; the collating sequence associated with alphabet-name-2 applies to key data items of class national' -- a rule that presupposes both may be established by one COLLATING SEQUENCE phrase. The claim's page reference '660' is the PRINTED page number (PDF 690), which checks out. A compiler built from the markdown alone would reject legal source.

CORROBORATION THAT THIS IS A TRANSCRIPTION DEFECT AND NOT AN ISO INCONSISTENCY. The two sibling figures for the same construct that have already been reconciled DO carry the bars in the markdown: SORT Format 1 at line 31458 ('COLLATING SEQUENCE  { {| FOR ALPHANUMERIC ... |}   }') with an explicit figure note at line 31474 spelling out the one-or-more semantics, and the file-level COLLATING SEQUENCE clause 12.4.5.7 at line 15186. MERGE is the unreconciled outlier.

I actively tried to refute this and could not: the bars are not reflowed elsewhere, the difference is not wrapping or page furniture, both sources are quoted accurately, and the meaning change is exactly the one 5.2.6.4 defines.
verdict.corrected_description:
The claim is accurate as written; no correction to its substance is needed. Two refinements for the ledger entry.

(1) Precise printed structure, for the fix: the outer delimiter is a BRACKET (whole clause optional); inside it a tall CURLY BRACE selects exactly one of two alternatives -- alternative 1 is the single line 'IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]', alternative 2 is a BRACE WITH CHOICE INDICATORS, i.e. one shorter curly '{' + bar on the left and bar + '}' on the right spanning BOTH FOR lines (it is one brace pair around the stack, not a separate brace per line as the ASCII stack currently suggests). Underlined (required) words in the printed figure: SEQUENCE, ALPHANUMERIC, NATIONAL; COLLATING, IS, and FOR are not underlined. A faithful transcription matching the already-reconciled SORT Format 1 style would be:

    [                      { IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]     } ]
    [ COLLATING SEQUENCE   { {| FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 |}  } ]
    [                      { {| FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2     |}  } ]

plus a figure note citing 5.2.6.4 and 14.9.24.4 general rule 5a.

(2) SIBLING DEFECTS found while verifying (out of scope for this claim, worth filing separately). (a) Same page 687, the OUTPUT PROCEDURE / GIVING group: the PDF encloses those two lines in a tall CURLY BRACE (exactly one shall be specified), but specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 28280-28282 render them as two independent optional BRACKETS '[ OUTPUT PROCEDURE ... ]' / '[ GIVING ... ]', which would wrongly permit neither or both. (b) SORT Format 2 (14.9.40, specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 31491, PDF page 776) has the identical missing-choice-indicator defect in its COLLATING SEQUENCE group. This is a pattern across the un-reconciled sort/merge figures, not a one-off.
